findings.title: Attendance timeline correction modal uses UTC string in local datetime input shifting timestamps
findings.scenario: Omar clocks out at 5:00 PM at Tom's pharmacy in Sydney. When Tom clicks to correct Omar's clock-out time on the review page, the date-time picker is populated with a universal time string showing 7:00 AM instead of 5:00 PM. When Tom submits the form, the browser parses the value in the local timezone, shifting the record 10 hours earlier so it precedes Omar's morning clock-in. The server rejects the submission for violating event order, blocking Tom from saving corrections, or silently distorts shift hours if editing clock-in.
findings.test_needed: In a browser running in Australia/Sydney (UTC+10), opening the correction modal for an event at 17:00 local time and submitting should send an effective timestamp of 17:00 AEST (07:00Z) rather than shifting 10 hours to 07:00 AEST (21:00Z previous day).

owner_question.question: When Tom corrects an attendance clock time on the review page, how should the date-time picker initialize and submit timestamps for Australian pharmacies?
options: (Recommended) Pre-fill the picker in the pharmacy's local timezone and submit the local time converted to UTC, preserving the intended hours.
Pre-fill the picker with UTC time and require managers to manually calculate timezone offsets.
Keep today's behaviour where UTC strings are loaded into local datetime pickers and shifted on submission.

findings.title: Shared shift landing redirect produces non-existent dashboard routes for non-standard roles
findings.scenario: Tom creates a shared shift link for an open shift at his pharmacy. When Lina, an organisation admin, clicks the link while logged in, the page calculates a non-existent role path. The application fails to match any valid screen and displays a missing page error, preventing Lina from reviewing the shift. The same breakdown locks out users with pharmacy manager roles.
findings.test_needed: Assert that an authenticated user with role ORG_STAFF or PHARMACY_MANAGER navigating to /shifts/link?token=... is not redirected to a non-existent route resulting in a 404 error.

owner_question.question: When Lina (organisation admin) or a pharmacy manager opens a shared shift link while logged in, where should the platform take them?
options: (Recommended) Redirect them to their organisation's shift center (/dashboard/organization/shifts/:id) or keep them on the shared shift details view.
Do not redirect logged-in admins away from the public shift view, rendering the shared shift directly.
Keep today's behaviour where they are redirected to /dashboard/orgstaff/shifts/:id resulting in a 404.
